name: settings-media-rows
description: the two media settings rows change the running browser at once, not only at the next launch. The staged fixture omits both keys (external-links-absent.settings.json's own pattern), so the window opens on the Rust core's own defaults (audible, background) rather than a value this scenario staged. Both edits go through eval + dispatchEvent rather than a CGEvent click, the pattern routing-pane-adds-a-rule.json already uses for a <select> and settings-external-links-row.json uses for a delegated-click control - a native <select> popup swallows a synthetic click, so this scenario never opens one. Reading the value back happens twice: once against the LIVE DOM right after each edit (no reload in between, which is what 'at once' means here) and once against settings.json on disk, so a build that repaints the row but never reaches the wire, or writes the file but never updates the live object, fails one half or the other.

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
Atrium MUST be frontmost or cmd+comma opens the frontmost app's own settings
open Settings on General; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
the window builds, the route loads, and the core's values land a beat after the labels

actions.expression: (() => { const a = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="autoMiniPlayer"] .settings-row-choice'); const c = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="controllerVisibility"] .settings-seg-option.on'); return `${a ? a.value : 'no-select'},${c ? c.dataset.choice : 'no-choice'}`; })()
actions.note: no fixture stages either key, so this must read the Rust core's own defaults

actions.expression: (() => { const select = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="autoMiniPlayer"] .settings-row-choice'); if (!select) return 'no-select'; select.value = 'anyVideo'; select.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); return 'changed'; })()
actions.note: settings.js reads the select's .value on change and sends the WHOLE object over settingsChanged, the same setRow path every other choice row uses
FAIL LOUDLY HERE: if the eval above missed the row, no save happens and the run stops at the edit that was wrong

actions.expression: (() => { const option = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="controllerVisibility"] .settings-seg-option[data-choice="always"]'); if (!option) return 'no-option'; option.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: the segmented shape - sidebarPosition and startupBehavior's own control - reached by its data-choice attribute rather than a screen coordinate
the second edit's own write, same reasoning as the first

actions.expression: (() => { const a = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="autoMiniPlayer"] .settings-row-choice'); const c = document.querySelector('.settings-row[data-key="controllerVisibility"] .settings-seg-option.on'); return `${a ? a.value : 'no-select'},${c ? c.dataset.choice : 'no-choice'}`; })()
actions.note: read straight off the same window, no relaunch and no reload of the pane in between - the 'at once' half

assertions.label: no-unusable-argument-refusal
assertions.pattern: Atrium: the settings surface sent an object the core
assertions.note: both rows send the WHOLE object; a partial one is refused by the core and the edit would never land

assertions.desc: the Rust core's own defaults, with no settings.json staged to override them
Both rows read back their new value in the SAME running window - the live change, not a relaunch
Cmd+Q still quits with the settings window open and two edits made
